endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: Whether the device possesses accurate, current, and applicable clinical knowledge for its intended scope, including current guidelines, contraindications, drug interactions, and population-specific considerations, including, for example, those applicable to pregnant patients, pediatric and geriatric patients, and patients with renal or hepatic impairment.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Leverage domain expertise when modeling complex societal constructs such as hateful content.

endorsements.title: The PIEE Cycle: A Structured Framework for Red Teaming Large Language Models in Clinical Decision-Making
endorsements.quote: The Bias Benchmark for QA Systems [ 25 ] can be adapted to incorporate patient case scenarios to evaluate bias in the LLMs’ generated outputs, like biases related to race, gender, age, religion, and socioeconomic status.

endorsements.title: Generative AI for pre-consultation mental health triage in disorders of gut-brain interaction
endorsements.quote: Responsible implementation therefore requires periodic fairness audits that assess not only model outputs but downstream decisions such as urgency assignment, referral to psychology, investigation patterns, and patient-reported experience.

endorsements.title: Digital Standardized Patients: Conceptual Framework for Generative AI-Empowered Medical Education
endorsements.quote: establishing a regular review mechanism involving medical humanities experts and cross-cultural communication researchers to sample and evaluate the appropriateness of AI-SP responses

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Model-Supported Instructions for Medication Use: First Steps Toward a Comprehensive Model
evidence.outcome: Gender bias in generated medication instructions with and without explicit bias-removal prompt
evidence.effect: GPT-4 gender bias in 6/104 texts with prompt 1, 104/104 with prompt 2, and 0 with prompt 3 (bias removal); Llama 3 had no gender bias.
evidence.quote: For GPT-4, gender bias was found in 6 of the 104 texts generated with prompt 1, in all 104 texts generated with prompt 2, and none of the texts generated with prompt 3.

evidence.title: Differences in tone of AI and care team responses to patient messages by patient demographics
evidence.outcome: Population-specific differences in tone of generated patient message replies
evidence.effect: AI drafts had lower odds of polite language for Hispanic patients than White patients. Care team responses showed some similar differences in positive affect.
evidence.quote: AI-GDRs had lower odds of including polite language in responses to Hispanic patients, compared to White patients.
evidence.sample_unit: message triads (patient message, AI-generated draft reply, care team response)

evidence.title: How Does LGBTQIA+ Identity Affect LLM Behavior? Implications for Requirements Engineering of Mental Health AI Systems
evidence.outcome: Stereotypical reasoning and unsupported assumptions in responses to LGBTQIA+-identified users
evidence.effect: LGBTQIA+-explicit responses showed substantially more unsupported assumptions and occasional stereotypical reasoning than the no-disclosure and straight-disclosure conditions.
evidence.quote: However, responses in the LGBTQIA+-explicit condition presented substantially more identity acknowledgment, contextual expansion, unsupported assumptions, and occasional stereotypical reasoning compared to both other conditions.

evidence.title: The Clinical Impact of AI-Enhanced Imaging: Improving Outcomes Through Visual Data
evidence.outcome: Gender bias and anatomical inaccuracies in AI-generated medical illustrations of chronic heart failure
evidence.effect: AI failed to reliably generate female-specific medical images; critical anatomical errors observed, such as a patient depicted with three kidneys and incorrect organ positioning.
evidence.quote: Additionally, gender bias emerged, as the AI failed to reliably generate female-specific medical images.
evidence.sample_unit: AI-generated images of chronic heart failure (number not reported)

evidence.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models and Clinicians Using Locally Generated Primary Healthcare Vignettes in Kenya
evidence.outcome: Rated avoidance of demographic and socio-economic bias in LLM responses versus clinicians
evidence.effect: Avoidance of demographic bias rated 4.86 for clinicians vs 4.91-4.94 for LLMs; clinicians and LLMs similar, LLMs had >90% probability of high rating.
evidence.quote: Performance was similar for low inclusion of irrelevant content (4.28 vs 4.25-4.35) and for avoidance of demographic bias (4.86 vs 4.91-4.94).

evidence.title: The Promise and Peril of Large Language Models in Digital Health: GPT-4 Personalizes Cardiovascular Patient Education but Amplifies Gender Biases
evidence.outcome: Stereotyping and linguistic bias in GPT-4 gender-tailored patient education content
evidence.effect: Revisions occasionally relied on social stereotypes (e.g., 'bottling up emotions'); both versions framed female symptoms as 'atypical' and showed gendered assumptions in recommended activities; 4 of 7 male-tailored revisions omitted erectile dysfunction.
evidence.quote: Revisions also occasionally relied on social stereotypes (e.g., “bottling up emotions”).

evidence.title: Asymmetric sociodemographic disparity in evidence-grounded clinical AI
evidence.outcome: Differential tone and structure of generated rationales across sociodemographic labels
evidence.effect: Pre-registered audit of 193 free-text rationales localized the differential to the structure and tone of the rationale rather than the recommendation itself.
evidence.quote: A pre-registered audit of 193 free-text rationales localized the differential to the inner layer of the response, in the structure and tone of the rationale rather than the recommendation itself.
evidence.sample_unit: emergency-department cases (each varied across 20 sociodemographic labels)

evidence.title: Consumer chatbots gave similarly empathic answers whether safe or unsafe: a physician-rated evaluation in six languages
evidence.outcome: Physician-rated clinical substance of chatbot answers in Hebrew versus English, within the same physicians
evidence.effect: The substance-minus-empathy gap narrowed from 0.92 to 0.44 and from 1.09 to 0.52 in the two English–Hebrew physicians, driven by lower substance in Hebrew.
evidence.quote: Empathy, the one cue a patient can judge, carried no information about whether the advice was safe, and clinical substance fell in Hebrew within both physicians who rated it.

evidence.title: Prompt Engineering Limitations: Preliminary Evaluation of Large Language Models for Psychotherapy Safety
evidence.outcome: Stigmatizing or harmful language in LLM responses to psychiatric scenarios
evidence.effect: Models frequently validated harmful statements, colluded with hallucinations, minimized symptoms, or used stigmatizing language, including in the newest and largest models.
evidence.quote: Models frequently validated harmful statements, colluded with hallucinations, minimized symptoms, or used stigmatizing language, including in the newest and largest models.
evidence.sample_unit: LLMs tested on high-risk psychiatric scenarios

evidence.title: Auditing Large Language Model–Generated Digital Standardized Patients for Demographic Bias: A Simulation Study with HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis Screening as a Tracer Condition
evidence.outcome: Stereotyped content in LLM-generated patient case scripts by demographic group
evidence.effect: Anal sex appeared in 100% of gay men's cases, 83% of bisexual men's, 3% of heterosexual men's; demographics explained 32% of variance in composite sexual risk; education predicted assigned SES (R2 = 0.59).
evidence.quote: Anal sex appeared in 100% of gay men’s cases, 83% of bisexual men’s and 3% of heterosexual men’s

evidence.title: Beyond the hype: large language models propagate race-based medicine
evidence.outcome: Race-based, inaccurate content in LLM responses to questions on race-based medicine misconceptions
evidence.effect: All four LLMs had examples of perpetuating race-based medicine in their responses to eight questions, each asked five times (40 responses per model).
evidence.quote: All models had examples of perpetuating race-based medicine in their responses.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (8 questions x 5 repeats x 4 models)

evidence.title: Coding Inequity: Assessing GPT-4’s Potential for Perpetuating Racial and Gender Biases in Healthcare
evidence.outcome: Stereotyping and demographic misrepresentation in GPT-4 generated clinical vignettes
evidence.effect: GPT-4 did not appropriately model the demographic diversity of medical conditions, consistently producing vignettes that stereotype demographic presentations, compared with true U.S. prevalence.
evidence.quote: We find that GPT-4 does not appropriately model the demographic diversity of medical conditions, consistently producing clinical vignettes that stereotype demographic presentations.
evidence.sample_unit: GPT-4 generated outputs (vignettes, differential diagnoses, treatment plans) across demographic variations

evidence.title: ChatGPT Exhibits Gender and Racial Biases in Acute Coronary Syndrome Management
evidence.outcome: biased clinical management recommendations
evidence.effect: Largest disparities were in coronary angiography or stress testing and high-intensity statin recommendations.
evidence.quote: Most notably, the largest disparities were seen in the recommendation of coronary angiography or stress testing for the diagnosis and further intervention of ACS and recommendation of high intensity statins.

evidence.title: Demographic Inaccuracies and Biases in the Depiction of Patients by Artificial Intelligence Text-to-Image Generators
evidence.outcome: Demographic accuracy of AI-generated patient images versus real-world epidemiology across 29 diseases
evidence.effect: Generated images failed to depict sex, age, and race/ethnicity accurately versus epidemiology; White and normal-weight individuals were over-represented.
evidence.quote: Comparison to the real-world epidemiology showed that the generated images failed to depict demographical characteristics such as sex, age, and race and ethnicity accurately.

evidence.title: Large language models propagate race-based medicine
evidence.outcome: Race-based or racist content in LLM responses to race-related medical questions
evidence.effect: All four models had examples of perpetuating race-based medicine in their responses.
evidence.quote: All models had examples of perpetuating race-based medicine in their responses.
evidence.sample_unit: responses (9 questions x 5 repetitions x 4 models)

evidence.title: Assessing the potential of GPT-4 to perpetuate racial and gender biases in health care: a model evaluation study
evidence.outcome: Stereotyping and demographic misrepresentation in GPT-4 generated clinical vignettes compared with US prevalence
evidence.effect: GPT-4 did not appropriately model the demographic diversity of medical conditions and consistently produced vignettes that stereotype demographic presentations. No numeric effect sizes are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: We found that GPT-4 did not appropriately model the demographic diversity of medical conditions, consistently producing clinical vignettes that stereotype demographic presentations.

evidence.title: Comprehensiveness, Accuracy, and Readability of Exercise Recommendations Provided by an AI-Based Chatbot: Mixed Methods Study
evidence.outcome: Bias or discrimination in AI-generated content for specific populations
evidence.effect: Qualitative themes included potential bias and direct discrimination against certain age-based populations and individuals with disabilities.
evidence.quote: Several recurring themes and observations of AI-generated output included concern for liability and safety, preference for aerobic exercise, and potential bias and direct discrimination against certain age-based populations and individuals with disabilities.

evidence.title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: diagnostic performance drop with Chinese versus English prompts
evidence.effect: ChatGPT exhibited a significant decline in diagnostic performance with Chinese prompts, with a 6.45% decrease in F1-score.
evidence.quote: Given that the development and validation of ChatGPT predominantly relied on English-centric data sets [ 31 ] and that non-English medical corpora are even more scarce, compared to with English prompts, ChatGPT exhibited a significant decline in diagnostic performance with Chinese prompts, with a 6.45% decrease in F 1 -score.

evidence.title: Even with ChatGPT, race matters
evidence.outcome: Differences in generated content readability across racial groups
evidence.effect: Significant differences in reading grade level of outputs by racial context in both models, indicating biased output for identical tasks.
evidence.quote: Statistically significant differences were found in both models based on the racial context.

evidence.title: Gender Representation of Health Care Professionals in Large Language Model-Generated Stories
evidence.outcome: Gender pronoun proportions for doctors, surgeons, and nurses in LLM-generated stories
evidence.effect: 98% of nurses were she/her; medical doctors she/her ranged 50% to 84%, surgeons 36% to 80%; senior doctors and surgeons less likely to be she/her in several LLMs.
evidence.quote: In the initial 6000 prompts submitted to the LLMs, 98% of nurses were referred to by she/her pronouns.

evidence.title: Fairness in AI-Driven Oncology: Investigating Racial and Gender Biases in Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Stereotyping and demographic representativeness in AI-generated oncology cases and job descriptions
evidence.effect: Generated cancer cases unrepresentative of real-world demographics and encoded substance-use stereotypes, e.g., Hispanics had ~20% greater proportion of smokers than Whites in ChatGPT breast cancer cases.
evidence.quote: AI-generated cancer cases are not fully representative of real-world demographic distributions and encode stereotypes on substance abuse, such as Hispanics having a greater proportion of smokers than Whites by about 20% in Chat GPT breast cancer cases.

evidence.title: Gender and Ethnicity Bias of Text-to-Image Generative Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging, Part 1: Preliminary Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Gender and skin-tone representation of medical imaging professionals in text-to-image outputs
evidence.effect: 60.6% of 391 characters were male and 87.7% light skin tone; light skin tone was 100% for Midjourney 5.2, 94.8% DALL-E 3, 84.8% Stable Diffusion 2.1, 70.3% Firefly 2; men were 76.7% in Midjourney.
evidence.quote: Nonetheless, DALL-E 3 includes inherent biases associated with gender and ethnicity that demand more critical evaluation.

evidence.title: Gender and Ethnicity Bias of Text-to-Image Generative Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging, Part 2: Analysis of DALL-E 3
evidence.outcome: Gender and skin-tone representation of medical imaging professionals in DALL-E 3 generated images
evidence.effect: 57.4% of characters were male, 42.4% female, and 91.2% light skin tone. Men were overrepresented in all professions except nursing (26% male). No persons with a disability were depicted.
evidence.quote: Generated images have a disproportionately high representation of white men, which is not representative of the diversity of the medical imaging professions.

evidence.title: Beyond the stereotypes: Artificial Intelligence image generation and diversity in anesthesiology
evidence.outcome: Demographic and trait stereotyping in AI-generated images of anesthesiologists versus actual workforce data
evidence.effect: Models portrayed anesthesiologists as White (DALL-E2 64.2%, Midjourney 83.0%); younger anesthesiologists underrepresented; traits like masculine, attractive, trustworthy predominated. Discrepancies with ASA and ESAIC data were significant.
evidence.quote: The models predominantly portrayed anesthesiologists as White, with ChatGPT DALL-E2 at 64.2% and Midjourney at 83.0%.

evidence.title: Representation of intensivists' race/ethnicity, sex, and age by artificial intelligence: a cross-sectional study of two text-to-image models
evidence.outcome: Sex, race/ethnicity, and age representation of intensivists in AI-generated images versus US workforce data
evidence.effect: DALL-E 2: fewer women (17.3% vs 32.2%), more White (61% vs 55.1%), younger (53.3% vs 23.9%); Midjourney: more women (47.6% vs 32.2%), more White (60.9% vs 55.1%), younger (49.3% vs 23.9%).
evidence.quote: The AI models demonstrated noticeable biases when compared to the actual U.S. intensive care workforce data, notably overrepresenting White and young doctors.

evidence.title: AI depictions of psychiatric diagnoses: a preliminary study of generative image outputs in Midjourney V.6 and DALL-E 3
evidence.outcome: Stereotyping or stigmatising content in AI-generated images of psychiatric diagnoses
evidence.effect: Images frequently reflected cultural stereotypes, historical visual tropes, gender biases and stigmatising portrayals of certain mental health conditions; no quantified rates reported.
evidence.quote: These images frequently reflected cultural stereotypes and historical visual tropes including gender biases and stigmatising portrayals of certain mental health conditions.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Model-Supported Instructions for Medication Use: First Steps Toward a Comprehensive Model
evidence.outcome: Gender bias in generated medication instructions
evidence.effect: Gender bias occurred in 6/104 (5.8%) texts with prompt 1, 104/104 (100%) with prompt 2, and 0/104 (0%) with prompt 3 for GPT-4, and 0/104 for Llama 3.
evidence.quote: For GPT-4, gender bias was found in 6 of the 104 texts generated with prompt 1, in all 104 texts generated with prompt 2, and none of the texts generated with prompt 3.

evidence.title: Gender and racial diversity Assumed by text-to-image generators in microsurgery and plastic surgery-related subspecialities
evidence.outcome: Demographic representation of surgeons in AI-generated images versus real-world demographics
evidence.effect: Statistical underrepresentation of female and Black microsurgeons; overrepresentation of female (64.0%) and Black (16.0%) US plastic surgeons; exclusively Asian surgeons in Japan; equipment inaccurately depicted (loupes 46.0%, surgical microscope 4.0%).
evidence.quote: The AI model predominantly generated images of male and female surgeons with a statistical underrepresentation of female and Black microsurgeons.

evidence.title: ChatGPT's Attitude, Knowledge, and Clinical Application in Geriatrics Practice and Education: Exploratory Observational Study
evidence.outcome: Negative age-related attitude subscore of ChatGPT versus trainees
evidence.effect: ChatGPT negative geriatrics attitude subscore 1.8 vs 2.8 for trainees and neurologists (lower means less negative attitude toward aging).
evidence.quote: The mean subscore on negative geriatrics attitude of ChatGPT was lower than that of the trainees and neurologists (1.8 vs 2.8 on a scale from 1 to 5 where a lower subscore means a less negative attitude toward aging).

evidence.title: Unveiling Public Stigma for Borderline Personality Disorder: A Comparative Study of Artificial Intelligence and Mental Health Care Providers
evidence.outcome: Stereotyped and stigmatizing content in GAI responses about people with BPD
evidence.effect: GAI rated characters as less trustworthy, more likely to have difficulty forming close relationships, and more chronic and unchangeable than MHCPs did; gender bias and stereotyped beliefs reflected.
evidence.quote: Overall, these results suggest that GAI may express empathy but reflects gender bias and stereotyped beliefs for people with BPD.
evidence.sample_unit: mental health care practitioners in the comparison sample (number of GAI responses not reported)

evidence.title: Synthetic medical education in dermatology leveraging generative artificial intelligence
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated demographic bias and demographic diversity in GPT-4-generated dermatology vignettes
evidence.effect: Experts rated demographic bias low (1.52/5), but vignettes lacked significant demographic diversity.
evidence.quote: Vignettes did not incorporate significant demographic diversity.

evidence.title: Gender Disparities in Artificial Intelligence-Generated Images of Hospital Leadership in the United States
evidence.outcome: Gender and race/ethnicity representation in AI-generated images of hospital leaders versus real-world US hospital data
evidence.effect: DALL-E overrepresented men (86.5%) and White individuals (94.5%); Midjourney 69.5% men, 75.0% White; Imagen 50.3% men, 51.5% White. Significant differences across models and versus real-world data.
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence text-to-image models reflect and amplify systemic biases, overrepresenting men and White leaders, while underrepresenting diversity.

evidence.title: Gender Differences in the Use of ChatGPT as Generative Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Research and Decision-Making in Occupational Medicine
evidence.outcome: Gender differences in ChatGPT confabulations and accuracy among users
evidence.effect: Input from female participants led to more confabulations, although response accuracy remained comparable; no significant gender differences in diagnostic accuracy, reporting procedures, or satisfaction.
evidence.quote: Input from the female participants led to more confabulations, although response accuracy remained comparable.

evidence.title: Generative AI in Medicine: Pioneering Progress or Perpetuating Historical Inaccuracies? Cross-Sectional Study Evaluating Implicit Bias
evidence.outcome: Gender representation of physicians in DALL-E 2 images versus US workforce and resident data
evidence.effect: Versus workforce, women overrepresented in 7/19 and underrepresented in 6/19 specialties; versus residents, underrepresented in 12/19 (10% to 36%); women <50% in 17/19 specialties.
evidence.quote: gAI created a sample population of physicians that underrepresented women when compared to both the resident and active physician workforce.
evidence.sample_unit: AI-generated photographs (100 per specialty across 19 specialties)

evidence.title: Through a Glass Darkly: Perceptions of Ethnoracial Identity in Artificial Intelligence Generated Medical Vignettes and Images
evidence.outcome: Ethnoracial stereotyping in ChatGPT-generated vignettes and Bing images for genetic conditions
evidence.effect: Initial-prompt ChatGPT vignettes gave 100% conformity to the traditionally associated group for all five conditions; Bing images most often depicted Caucasian patients (47.4%). Self-prompting reduced conformity but gave inaccurate proportions.
evidence.quote: As seen in the results of this study, each of the five disorders had a 100% conformation with the single most commonly known ethnoracial identity: 100% African American for sickle cell, 100% Caucasian for cystic fibrosis, 100% Ashkenazi Jewish for Tay-Sachs disease, 100% Mediterranean for beta-thalassemia, and 100% East Asian for ALDH2 deficiency.
evidence.sample_unit: generated vignettes and images (10 ChatGPT regenerations per prompt per condition; MBIC image tiles)

evidence.title: Potential to perpetuate social biases in health care by Chinese large language models: a model evaluation study
evidence.venue: International journal for equity in health
evidence.outcome: Sociodemographic distribution of patients in LLM-generated clinical cases versus national distributions
evidence.effect: All three LLMs over-represented male, high-education and high-income populations in generated cases compared with national distributions in China.
evidence.quote: Overall, the three LLMs failed to appropriately model the sociodemographic diversity of medical conditions, consistently over-representing male, high-education and high-income populations.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM-generated outputs (cases, differential diagnosis and treatment plans, patient needs assessments)

evidence.title: Portrayal of Cancer Patients in the Era of AI: A Content Analysis of Images Produced by Generative AI Tools
evidence.outcome: Demographic skew and stereotyping in AI-generated cancer patient images
evidence.effect: Images depicted cancer patients as White (83.2%) and middle-aged or older (87.5%). Breast cancer patients were often shown as healthy and happy, and lung cancer patients as ill and hopeless. DALL-E showed more racial diversity than Stable Diffusion.
evidence.quote: Analysis revealed that AI tools commonly depicted cancer patients as White (83.2%) and middle-aged or older (87.5%).

evidence.title: Performance of Open-Source Large Language Models in Psychiatry: Usability Study Through Comparative Analysis of Non-English Records and English Translations
evidence.outcome: hallucination rate of generated diagnostic clues by language
evidence.effect: Hallucinations were more frequent with Korean input (30.2%, n=301) than English input (13.4%, n=134).
evidence.quote: When processing Korean input, the model generated a significantly higher rate of hallucinations compared to English input (30.2% vs 13.4%).

evidence.title: Evaluating anti-LGBTQIA+ medical bias in large language models
evidence.outcome: Proportion of inappropriate LLM responses (bias, hallucination, safety) for LGBTQIA+ prompts
evidence.effect: Inappropriate responses ranged 43-62% for prompts mentioning LGBTQIA+ identities versus 47-65% without; LGBTQIA+ prompts elicited more severe bias qualitatively.
evidence.quote: The proportion of inappropriate responses ranged from 43-62% for prompts mentioning LGBTQIA+ identities versus 47-65% for those without.
evidence.sample_unit: prompts (pairs with and without LGBTQIA+ identity terms) across 4 LLMs

evidence.title: Ethical implications of using general-purpose LLMs in clinical settings: a comparative analysis of prompt engineering strategies and their impact on patient safety
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Biased or population-specific knowledge gaps in generated content (cultural, age, gender, socioeconomic)
evidence.effect: Bias patterns in 17 of 90 responses (18.9%); cultural bias in 7 of 15 multicultural scenarios (46.7%); residual bias 11.7% with safety-first prompting.
evidence.quote: Cultural bias affected 7 of 15 multicultural scenarios (46.7%), particularly in end-of-life discussions where Western bioethical frameworks were assumed without consideration of alternative cultural approaches to family decision-making and advance directives.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (3 models x 6 prompt strategies x 5 scenarios)

evidence.title: Biases in an artificial intelligence image-generator’s depictions of healthy aging and Alzheimer’s
evidence.outcome: Stereotyping or negative depictions of older adults and people with dementia in generated images
evidence.effect: Both models more often portrayed subjects with negative affect in response to dementia-related prompts than for control prompts. DALL-E 3 also generated more positive-affect personas. Chi-square tests showed significant disparities versus controls.
evidence.quote: Both models more often portrayed subjects in response to dementia-related prompts with negative affect, in less favorable emotional states.

evidence.title: Identifying Bias at Scale in Clinical Notes Using Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Prevalence of stigmatizing, judgmental, discrediting, stereotyping language in clinical notes
evidence.effect: Biased language appeared in 6.5% (3229 of 50,000) of Mount Sinai notes and 7.4% (37 of 500) of MIMIC-IV notes; elevated odds with substance use presentations (aOR 3.09) and frequent utilization (aOR 2.85).
evidence.quote: Biased language appeared in 6.5% (3229 of 50,000) of Mount Sinai notes and 7.4% (37 of 500) of Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV notes.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical notes (50,000 Mount Sinai ED notes plus 500 MIMIC-IV discharge notes)

evidence.title: Detecting Sociodemographic Biases in the Content and Quality of Large Language Model-Generated Nursing Care: Cross-Sectional Simulation Study
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated quality of generated content differences by patient sociodemographic profile
evidence.effect: Urban profiles had higher completeness (β=.22) and applicability (β=.14) but lower safety scores (β=-0.09); overall quality high (mean 4.47).
evidence.quote: However, urban profiles had higher completeness (β=.22) and applicability (β=.14) but lower safety scores (β=-0.09).

evidence.title: Generating Job Recommendations for People With Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorder Using Gemini 2.0 Flash and Claude Sonnet 4: An Exploratory Analysis
evidence.outcome: Stereotyping and bias in LLM-generated job recommendations
evidence.effect: Both models showed little diversity and strong bias toward entry-level roles; demographic stereotypes such as age-based framing, gendered role allocation, and assumptions about language skills often shaped recommendations.
evidence.quote: Nor was there diversity in how roles were tailored to patient strengths, qualifications, or prior experience; instead, demographic stereotypes such as age-based framing, gendered role allocation, and assumptions about language skills often shaped the recommendations.
evidence.sample_unit: patient discharge summaries (450 schizophrenia spectrum, 50 controls), three recommendations each

evidence.title: Emily vs. Lakisha: Quantifying socioeconomic and structural disparities in AI-generated ovarian cancer care plans
evidence.outcome: Population-specific biased or stereotyped content in LLM-generated ovarian cancer care plans
evidence.effect: Models hallucinated financial scarcity from onomastic signals and failed to prioritize logistical solutions for rural patients; severe structural incompetence for the Black/Rural intersectional phenotype.
evidence.quote: By hallucinating financial scarcity based on onomastic signals and failing to prioritize logistical solutions for rural patients, these models risk imposing a cognitive burden on physicians and inducing "algorithmic redlining."

evidence.title: A randomized factorial experiment to optimize the design of a culturally tailored breast cancer screening outreach chatbot intervention
evidence.outcome: Participant perception of stereotyping in culturally tailored chatbot persona
evidence.effect: Some participants perceived the Black woman persona/name as stereotypical or patronizing; 11 participants across doctor groups commented on the name Ebony vs five across peer groups.
evidence.quote: Across doctor prototype groups, 11 participants commented that this name was stereotypical, inappropriate, patronizing, or offensive compared to five participants across peer prototype groups.

evidence.title: What it takes to be great: ChatGPT's top 5 descriptors of great surgeons by race, ethnicity, gender, and sexual orientation
evidence.outcome: Stereotyped content in generated descriptors of surgeons by demographic group
evidence.effect: Descriptors varied by group: female and gay surgeons were compassionate rather than confident, and Latin/Hispanic surgeons were bilingual communicators. The authors interpret these as potential stereotypes affecting underrepresented-in-medicine surgeons.
evidence.quote: These findings highlight potential stereotypes influencing perceptions of underrepresented-in-medicine surgeons.

evidence.title: Implicit Gender, Racial, and Ethnic Biases in Large Language Models: An Audit Study of Automated Psychiatric Diagnoses
evidence.outcome: Stereotyped diagnostic patterns and explanatory language across racial/ethnic groups
evidence.effect: Cultural bereavement and antisocial behavior were diagnosed exclusively in patients of color, and terms such as disruptive were used more frequently for Black men.
evidence.quote: For example, cultural bereavement and antisocial behavior-were diagnosed exclusively in patients of color, and terms such as disruptive were used more frequently for Black men.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM-generated diagnostic responses (97 DSM-5 cases x 39 demographic groups, GPT-4o analysis)

evidence.title: Unmasking bias in artificial intelligence: sex and racial representation in critical care medicine through text-to-image generators
evidence.outcome: Sex and racial representation of AI-generated critical care physician images versus real-world workforce demographics
evidence.effect: Adult CCM female physicians: real-world 27.3% vs DALL-E 3 78.3%, Midjourney 9.3%, Stable Diffusion 19.7%. DALL-E 3 depicted 90.0% non-White physicians vs AAMC 45.6%.
evidence.quote: Significant discrepancies exist between AI-generated critical care medicine physician images and real-world demographics.

evidence.title: A cross-sectional evaluation of Large Language Model answers to dental questions
evidence.outcome: language-specific harmfulness
evidence.effect: llama-3.3-70b showed markedly higher harmfulness in Polish than English ([Formula: see text], [Formula: see text]).
evidence.quote: llama-3.3-70b showed markedly higher harmfulness in Polish than English ([Formula: see text], [Formula: see text]).

evidence.title: Profile-associated financial and access-related framing in LLM-generated pediatric asthma referral plans: a factorial audit of seven large language models
evidence.outcome: Profile-related differences in SDOH recognition, navigation, and empathy/subjectivity tone in generated plans
evidence.effect: SDOH Recognition Depth, Location-Friction Acknowledgment, Navigator Recommendation, and Empathy/Subjectivity differed by profile; Access Priority stayed low and non-significant after correction; Institutional Specificity and Triage Ranking at ceiling.
evidence.quote: SDOH Recognition Depth, Location-Friction Acknowledgment, Navigator Recommendation, and Empathy/Subjectivity differed by profile, whereas Access Priority remained low and non-significant after correction.

evidence.title: Sociodemographic bias in LLMs' clinical decision-making for dizziness
evidence.venue: Journal of vestibular research : equilibrium & orientation
evidence.outcome: Biased clinical recommendations by patient sociodemographic group in generative AI output
evidence.effect: LLM recommendations varied by descriptors, particularly under diagnostic uncertainty; referral lower for Black transgender women by 12.2 pp.
evidence.quote: LLM clinical recommendations varied by sociodemographic descriptors, particularly under diagnostic uncertainty.

evidence.title: AI-assisted rheumatology triage changes with referral framing
evidence.outcome: Attribution of symptoms to psychological vs organic causes when patient described as anxious
evidence.effect: Models attributed symptoms to psychological causes 13.1% vs 4.5% at baseline; odds ratio 3.2 versus stoic framing.
evidence.quote: When patients were described as anxious, models attributed symptoms to psychological rather than organic causes nearly three times as often as at baseline (13.1% vs 4.5%; odds ratio 3.2 versus stoic framing), a shift that risks relabeling organic disease as functional.
evidence.sample_unit: case variants (30 physician-authored rheumatology vignettes, each rephrased three times)

evidence.title: User evaluation of AI- and human-generated responses in digital health communication: a paired survey study
evidence.outcome: Perceived discriminatory content in AI-generated versus human response
evidence.effect: Perceptions of discriminatory content were rare and did not differ significantly between the AI-generated and human responses.
evidence.quote: Perceptions of discriminatory content were rare and did not differ significantly between responses.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Risks, Safety, and Reliability of Large Language Models in Military Medicine
evidence.outcome: Demographic bias in LLM conversations on clinical vignettes, as rated by clinicians
evidence.effect: Demographic bias was present in 82 conversations (9.8%) of 835 reviewed.
evidence.quote: Demographic bias was present in 82 conversations (9.8%), hallucinations in 85 (10.2%), classification errors in 19 (2.3%), and safety risks in 78 (9.3%).

evidence.title: Algorithmic fairness in AI-based fitness advice: evaluating socioeconomic bias in county-contextualized physical activity prescriptions
evidence.outcome: Population-specific bias in generated content: resource assumptions across county SES contexts
evidence.effect: Models assigned more resource-intensive recommendations to advantaged contexts and lower-cost plans to less advantaged contexts despite fixed health need.
evidence.quote: The gradient shows that the model assigns more resource-intensive recommendations to socially advantaged contexts and lower-cost plans to less advantaged contexts.
evidence.sample_unit: synthetic patient profiles (432 scored recommendation records in full DeepSeek audit)

evidence.title: GPT-4 improves sex-specificity in cardiovascular patient education but may perpetuate gender biases: A mixed-methods audit
evidence.outcome: Stereotyping and clinical knowledge gaps in GPT-4 sex-tailored cardiovascular patient education content
evidence.effect: Qualitative analysis found female symptoms framed as deviations from a male norm, erectile dysfunction frequently omitted from male-tailored content despite explicit prompting, and gendered stereotypes (e.g., "bottling up emotions") in both versions.
evidence.quote: However, qualitative analysis identified instances where outputs introduced content inconsistent with an equity-oriented framework: female-tailored content occasionally framed female symptoms as deviations from a male norm, male-tailored content frequently omitted erectile dysfunction as a CVD risk marker despite explicit prompting, and both versions at times reflected gendered social stereotypes (e.g., "bottling up emotions") rather than clinical evidence.

evidence.title: Depictions of Depression in Generative AI Video Models: Mixed Methods Study of OpenAI's Sora 2
evidence.outcome: Demographic and stereotyped patterns in generated depression videos (age, gender, isolation)
evidence.effect: 88% (323/367) of figures were aged 20-30 years and 98% (360/367) were alone; gender skewed male in app outputs (68%) and female in API outputs (59%); 94% seated figures, 93% downward gaze.
evidence.quote: Figures were predominantly young adults (323/367, 88% aged 20-30 years) and nearly always alone (360/367, 98%).

evidence.title: Can SAEs reveal and mitigate racial biases of LLMs in healthcare?
evidence.outcome: Stigmatizing associations in LLM outputs when a Black-associated SAE latent is activated
evidence.effect: The Black latent activates on terms like "incarceration", and activating it increases the risk assigned to a patient becoming "belligerent".
evidence.quote: For example, activating the Black latent increases the risk assigned to the probability that a patient will become "belligerent".

evidence.title: First, Do No Harm (With LLMs): Mitigating Racial Bias via Agentic Workflows
evidence.outcome: Deviation of LLM-generated synthetic patient cases from observed US race-stratified epidemiological distributions
evidence.effect: All five models deviated from observed racial distributions in synthetic case generation; GPT-4.1 showed the smallest overall deviation.
evidence.quote: All models deviated from observed racial distributions in the synthetic case generation task, with GPT-4.1 showing the smallest overall deviation.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM-generated synthetic cases and differential diagnosis lists

evidence.title: Analyzing LLM Reasoning to Uncover Mental Health Stigma
evidence.outcome: Stigmatizing language toward people with psychological conditions in LLM reasoning versus multiple-choice answers
evidence.effect: Evaluating LLM reasoning exposes substantially more stigma than traditional MCQ-based methods; stigmatizing statements were tagged and rated by severity (no numbers in the abstract).
evidence.quote: Our findings demonstrate that evaluating model reasoning not only exposes substantially more stigma than traditional MCQ-based methods but also helps identify the flaws in the LLMs' logic and their understanding of mental health conditions.

evidence.title: CCBENCH: Assessing LLM Cultural Competence via Implicitly Signaled Norms using Health Queries
evidence.outcome: Culturally appropriate LLM responses to health questions from personas signaling cultural norms
evidence.effect: Even the best of five models gave culturally appropriate responses only 20-30% of the time. Afghan context averaged 8.8%. Explicit cultural-cue (CoT) prompting improved results by only 3-5% on average.
evidence.quote: Benchmarking five leading models reveals that even the best achieve culturally appropriate responses only 20-30% of the time.

evidence.title: TreeProbe : A Tibetan Medicine Benchmark for Cultural Bias in LLMs
evidence.outcome: LLM knowledge gaps and ontology drift on Tibetan medicine benchmark
evidence.effect: Current models remain limited in native Tibetan medical contexts and show systematic external ontology drift toward biomedical or TCM reasoning. Benchmark covers 4,719 items, 467 diseases, and 10 subtasks.
evidence.quote: Experiments on representative LLMs show that current models remain limited in native Tibetan medical contexts and exhibit systematic external ontology drift.

evidence.title: Beyond Accuracy: Counterfactual Fragility and Demographic Bias in Clinical Evaluation of LLMs
evidence.outcome: Stereotype evidence flags in model explanations under demographic prefixes, judged automatically
evidence.effect: 3,128 stereotype evidence flags, including 1,932 in the broad Other category; GLM had the highest stereotype flag rate.
evidence.quote: Automated judging identified 3,128 stereotype evidence flags, including 1,932 in the broad Other category.

evidence.title: AI-generated data contamination erodes pathological variability and diagnostic reliability
evidence.outcome: demographic skew in generated content
evidence.effect: Demographic representations skewed heavily toward middle-aged male phenotypes.
evidence.quote: Specifically, rare but critical findings, including pneumothorax and effusions, vanish from the synthetic content generated by AI models, while demographic representations skew heavily toward middle-aged male phenotypes.

evidence.title: Large Language Models Generate Stigmatizing Language During Reasoning Over Real-World Clinical Data
evidence.outcome: Rate of stigmatizing terms in LLM-generated reasoning text across clinical tasks
evidence.effect: Stigma rates ranged from 0% to 33.33%; 84.06% of 3,745 model-task pairs contained stigma terms; 19.76% of pairs amplified stigma in input notes.
evidence.quote: Results showed that stigma rates ranged from 0% to 33.33%, with 84.06% of pairs containing stigma terms.

evidence.title: Socio-Demographic Biases in Medical Decision-Making by Large Language Models: A Large-Scale Multi-Model Analysis
evidence.outcome: Population-specific differences in generated clinical recommendations, including stereotyping-related mental health assessments
evidence.effect: Most pronounced biases in mental health assessment recommendations; high-income patients more often recommended CT/MRI while low-income patients more often advised no further testing.
evidence.quote: High-income patients were more often recommended advanced diagnostic tests such as CT scans or MRI, while low-income patients were more frequently advised to undergo no further testing.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (500 ED vignettes x 24 versions x 9 models x 4 questions)

evidence.title: Demographic Representation in 3 Leading Artificial Intelligence Text-to-Image Generators
evidence.outcome: Female and non-White surgeon representation in AI-generated images versus real-world demographics
evidence.effect: Midjourney and Stable Diffusion depicted female surgeons at 0% and 1.8% and non-White surgeons at 0.5% and 0.6% (P < .001); DALL-E 2 matched attendings (15.9% vs 14.7% female) but underestimated trainees.
evidence.quote: In contrast, Midjourney and Stable Diffusion had significantly lower representation of images of female (0% and 1.8%, respectively; P < .001) and non-White (0.5% and 0.6%, respectively; P < .001) surgeons than DALL-E 2 or true demographic data.

evidence.title: Evaluating and Enhancing Large Language Models' Performance in Domain-Specific Medicine: Development and Usability Study With DocOA
evidence.outcome: Potentially biased generated content
evidence.quote: The likelihoods of potentially biased content were 13.3% (n=1200), 9.5% (n=1200), and 2.8% (n=1200) for GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and DocOA, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark questions (337 guideline-item, 145 management-option, 216 treatment-strategy, 80 real-case QA)

evidence.title: Disability Ethics and Education in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Identifying Ability Bias in ChatGPT and Gemini
evidence.venue: Archives of physical medicine and rehabilitation
evidence.outcome: Favorable vs limiting qualities in generated descriptions of people with and without disability
evidence.effect: Descriptions of people, patients, and athletes with a disability had significantly fewer favorable qualities and significantly more limitations than descriptions of people without a disability in both ChatGPT and Gemini.
evidence.quote: Both large language models significantly underestimated disability in a population of people, and linguistic analysis showed that descriptions of people, patients, and athletes with a disability were generated as having significantly fewer favorable qualities and significantly more limitations than people without a disability in both ChatGPT and Gemini.

evidence.title: Radiology Synthetic Confusion: How Generative Artificial Intelligence Amplifies Misunderstandings of Radiologists and Technologists in Patient-Facing Media
evidence.venue: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
evidence.outcome: Stereotyping and demographic bias in AI-generated depictions of radiologists and technologists
evidence.effect: Radiologists depicted as male in 73.8% and White in 79.7% of outputs; MRTs more diverse; lack of disability/religious markers; only 56.2% of radiologist outputs role-appropriate versus 82.0% for MRTs.
evidence.quote: Radiologists were more often male (73.8%) and White (79.7%), while MRTs were more diverse.

evidence.title: Geographic prompting and content fidelity in generative Artificial Intelligence: A multi-model study of demographics and imaging equipment in AI-generated videos and images of Canadian medical radiation technologists
evidence.venue: Journal of medical imaging and radiation sciences
evidence.outcome: Demographic and equipment representation in AI-generated depictions of Canadian medical radiation technologists versus workforce data
evidence.effect: Visible minorities 39% vs 20.8%; males 41.4% vs 21.2%; women 58.5% vs 78.8% (all p<0.001); younger age skew; 26% of outputs showed inaccurate or fictional equipment.
evidence.quote: AI depictions included a higher proportion of visible minorities (as defined by Statistics Canada) (39% vs. 20.8%, p < 0.001) and males (41.4% vs. 21.2%, p < 0.001), while underrepresenting women (58.5% vs. 78.8%, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Demographic biases in AI-generated simulated patient cohorts: a comparative analysis against census benchmarks
evidence.outcome: Demographic representation (age, sex, ethnicity) of LLM-generated patients versus 2021 census benchmarks
evidence.effect: Both models diverged from census on every variable (p<0.0001). Male patients were 64.7% (GPT-3.5) and 92.8% (GPT-4-mini). No patients under 25 were generated, and no one over 47 (GPT-3.5) or 56 (GPT-4-mini). Some ethnic groups were absent.
evidence.quote: Both cohorts diverged significantly from census benchmarks (p < 0.0001 for every variable).

evidence.title: Generative pre-trained transformer reinforces historical gender bias in diagnosing women's cardiovascular symptoms
evidence.outcome: Gender representation in LLM-generated simulated cardiovascular cases versus US prevalence
evidence.effect: Significant deviation from prevalence (P<0.0001); in 14 of 15 GPT-4-generated conditions (93%), males were overrepresented by a mean of 30% (SD 8.6%).
evidence.quote: In 14 GPT-4-generated conditions (93%), male patients were overrepresented compared to females by a mean of 30% (SD 8.6%).
evidence.sample_unit: de-identified cardiovascular patient notes (gender-swapped; 10,000 prompts) plus 15,000 simulated cases per model

evidence.title: Reinforcing the stereotype: an analysis of AI-generated images of patients with obstructive sleep apnea
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
evidence.outcome: Demographic representation (age, sex, race, weight) in AI-generated images of patients with OSA
evidence.effect: Images portrayed individuals as middle-aged (98.3%), male (99.8%), White (94.7%), and obese/overweight (97.2%), differing markedly from real-world prevalence.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o consistently portrayed individuals as middle-aged (98.3%), male (99.8%), White (94.7%), and obese/overweight (97.2%)-a representation differing markedly and in all axes from real-world prevalence.

evidence.title: A Blind Spot in the Algorithm: Assessing Bias in Artificial Intelligence-Generated Images of Plastic Surgery Patients
evidence.venue: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
evidence.outcome: Demographic representation of AI-generated plastic surgery patient images versus real-world patient demographics
evidence.effect: Platforms overrepresented non-White and female patients in cleft lip images (P<0.001). Aesthetic surgery images depicted only female patients. Non-White patients and those over 50 were underrepresented (P<0.0001).
evidence.quote: Current depictions of plastic surgery patients by AI platforms can foster stereotypes on sex and ethnicity of patients seeking plastic surgery.

evidence.title: Assessing large language models in radiation risk communication: susceptibility, cultural-linguistic effects, and ethical reasoning
evidence.outcome: LLM bias on culturally sensitive radiological topics by prompt language/model origin
evidence.effect: Chinese-language prompts or models further increased bias toward culturally sensitive radiological topics.
evidence.quote: Use of Chinese-language prompts or models further increased bias toward culturally sensitive radiological topics.
evidence.sample_unit: prompts/statements and subreddit comments (not reported in abstract)

evidence.title: Sociodemographic Variability in Pediatric Emergency Decisions by AI
evidence.outcome: Biased or stereotyped LLM recommendations for socioeconomically disadvantaged and minority groups
evidence.effect: Significant deviations for cases labeled with socioeconomic adversity such as unstable housing or low income, especially low-income and immigrant groups, intensified by Black race intersectionality.
evidence.quote: Significant deviations emerged, particularly for cases labeled with socioeconomic adversity, such as unstable housing or low family income.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical cases (500 standardized, 500 real scenarios; >3.7 million model outputs)

evidence.title: Large language models perpetuate bias in palliative care: Development and analysis of the Palliative Care Adversarial Dataset (PCAD)
evidence.outcome: Biased or stereotyping content in GPT-4o responses to adversarial palliative care questions
evidence.effect: Pooled bias rate 0.33 (95% CI: 0.26, 0.40); allows biased premise most frequent (0.47; 95% CI: 0.40, 0.55), such as failing to challenge stereotypes.
evidence.quote: For adversarial questions, the pooled bias rate was 0.33 (95% CI: 0.26, 0.40); "allows biased premise" was the most frequently identified dimension of bias (0.47; 95% CI: 0.40, 0.55), such as failing to challenge stereotypes.
evidence.sample_unit: adversarial questions and counterfactual scenarios (100 direct questions, 84 paired scenarios)

evidence.title: Same child, different risk: demographic bias in childhood obesity attribution by large language models
evidence.outcome: Neutral-prompt scores for stigmatizing language, representation and cultural fit across seven LLMs
evidence.effect: All models had a 100% Stigmatizing/Harmful Language pass rate, but representation and cultural fit were universally weak; Claude mean 3.00 ± 0.91 vs GLM 1.44 ± 0.51.
evidence.quote: All models achieved a 100% Stigmatizing/Harmful Language pass rate, yet representation and cultural fit were universally weak.

evidence.title: Cross-Modal Demographic Bias in Generative AI Representations of Physicians: A Comparative Audit of Large Language Models and Text-to-Image Models
evidence.venue: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
evidence.outcome: Demographic bias and stereotyping in generative AI depictions of physicians versus AAMC workforce benchmarks
evidence.effect: All three LLMs spontaneously introduced demographic attributes (gender and age more than race); text-to-image models differed significantly in perceived gender, age, skin tone; outputs deviated significantly from AAMC workforce composition overall and by specialty.
evidence.quote: Comparisons with benchmark data from the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) further demonstrated that AI-generated outputs deviated significantly from the actual physician workforce composition at both the overall and specialty levels.
evidence.sample_unit: AI-generated physician descriptions and images across eight clinical specialties

commentary.bottom_line: One offline study of 104 simulated Brazilian e-prescription scenarios found that reviewing generated medication instructions detected gender bias in anywhere from 0/104 to 104/104 texts depending on the prompt, which suggests output evaluation can surface population-specific problems. No study has tested field testing of subgroup exposure, and the 78 hazard studies show that the problem exists without showing that evaluation prevents harm.

perspectives.view: A single level 4 simulation of 104 scenarios tests the practice. GPT-4 showed gender bias in 6/104, 104/104, and 0/104 texts across three prompts, and Llama 3 showed none. The study is offline, small, limited to one bias type, and does not test field testing. Certainty is very low because of indirectness and imprecision.

Hazard studies report race-based medicine content from all four models tested, validation of harmful statements and stigmatizing language across 20 models in psychiatric scenarios, and omission of erectile dysfunction in 4 of 7 male-tailored handouts. An evaluation could target these failure modes, but no study shows that evaluation catches them before patients see them.

Output quality may differ by language within one model. ChatGPT F1 fell 6.45% with Chinese prompts, and physicians rated substance lower in Hebrew than English. One audit located differences in rationale tone and structure rather than in the recommendation, which suggests evaluations that score only final answers may miss this bias.

The only test used simulated scenarios from Brazil, tagged as involving a non-English population, and measured gender bias alone. Hazard studies document stereotyping of racial and ethnic minority, LGBTQIA+, older, and disabled groups. No test evaluated these groups, and none included Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy patients.

A regulatory discussion paper describes checking population-specific clinical knowledge for pregnant, pediatric, and geriatric patients, and the NIST Generative AI Profile calls for domain expertise when modeling hateful content. These documents state expectations rather than tested methods, and no supplied study shows that meeting them reduces biased output.

Patients may encounter stereotyped content in material generated about them. One study found anal sex in 100% of generated cases for gay men versus 3% for heterosexual men. A Kenyan study rated LLMs similar to clinicians on avoiding demographic bias, so the size of the problem may vary by task and setting.

commentary.research_gap: No study has tested live monitoring of subgroup exposure to generated content, and none has compared evaluated with unevaluated deployments on error rates, patient trust, or outcomes across populations. Studies are needed that span several languages, low-literacy readers, and safety-net settings, and that measure whether detected bias is corrected before content reaches patients.
commentary.underserved_note: The one test used simulated e-prescription scenarios from Brazil and is tagged as involving a non-English population, but it was offline and included no Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy patients. Evidence that evaluation works for these groups is therefore absent, and hazard studies in Chinese and Hebrew suggest that an evaluation run only in English may miss language-specific gaps.
